newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - April 23.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - April 23.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, the Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
PARIS - Spending on advertising in western Europe is likely to rise by 4.9 percent in 1997 compared with 1996, according to the annual Europub review published by French communications group Havas.

BERLIN - Decision by London-based advertising and marketing group Cordiant Plc to demerge into three independently managed businesses is welcomed by two of its units in Germany, Europe's biggest advertising market. Directors of Bates and Scholz & Friends says Cordiant dissolution will boost growth by freeing them to compete and respond to client needs more effectively.

LONDON - British millionaire businessman Paul Sykes is to launch a one million pound ($1.6 million) newspaper advertising campaign urging opponents of a single European currency to vote Conservative in the May 1 election reports the Financial Times.

MUNICH, Germany - German private television channel Pro Sieben says it boosted gross advertising income in the first quarter of 1997 by 18 percent -- to 641 million marks -- placing it among the top three German TV stations for growth.

DETROIT - Ford Motor Co is consolidating national media buying for its U.S. operations through an agency buying organisation called Ford Motor Media. The new organisation is a wholly owned subsidiary of J. Walter Thompson USA.

LONDON - British television networks refuse to transmit an "offensive" anti-abortion election broadcast showing dead foetuses. The BBC says the election broadcast by the Pro-Life Alliance, a single-issue party with 56 election candidates, is "offensive under BBC guidelines and cannot be transmitted in its present form".

LONDON - British advertising and marketing services group, WPP Group Plc, buys stake in Syzygy, a London-based digital media company. The investment means WPP now owns or has stakes in six new media companies, as part of a strategy to offer clients interactive media options.

KRONBERG, Germany - The growth of the German advertising market is slowing down, media marketing company IP Deutschland says. IP Deutschland predict net spending for media, cinema and billboard advertising will increase by only 1.9 percent to 32.8 billion marks ($19.2 billion), below the expected 2.5 percent expansion of the German economy for 1997.
BOSTON - A gay rights group previews a 30-second commercial about job discrimination that it had hoped to air on the hit television show "Ellen," but ABC, the U.S. network, turned it down.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:
FRANKFURT - German media companies and publishers are spending an increasing amount of money on consumer market research, the German Working Group of Market and Social Research Institutes says.
WASHINGTON - The Washington Post Co says second-half results will be adversely affected by the lack of political and Olympic advertising that benefited it in late 1996.

HELSINKI - A battle for market share in Nordic media takes a new turn as Finnish media group Aamulehti Yhtyma Oy, facing mounting competition from local rival Sanoma Oy, says it will merge with domestic broadcaster MTV Oy.
PARIS - Next year will see the launch of the first of three satellites owned by WorldSpace Inc which aims to offer digital audio broadcasting radio through space.
SYDNEY - Australian Communications Minister Richard Alston, overseeing a review of media ownership controls, says any changes to ownership limits must be in the national interest.
LONDON - Britain's Independent Television Commission criticises the ITV commercial network for an over-reliance on drama and calls on it to boost its comedy programming.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

HANOI - U.S. beverage giant Coca-Cola says the authorities in Vietnam's Ho Chi Minh City have denied the company permission to run a promotion campaign which offered mountain bikes as prizes. The company says it was rejected because, in the opinion of the local Service of Trade, the chances of winning were too low.
TOKYO - Honda Motor Co Ltd says it is studying whether to take a stake in the Sino-French Guangzhou Peugeot Automobile joint venture.

WASHINGTON - Suzuki Motor Corp. escalates its feud with the Consumers Union, claiming that its once popular Samurai sports-utility vehicle was set up to fail in a flawed 1988 swerve test conducted by the group.

ORLANDO, Florida - Planet Hollywood International Inc and Saudi Arabia's Prince Alwaleed Bin Talal Bin Abdulaziz Al Saud say they have formed a strategic pact in which the prince would develop up to 34 Planet restaurant-merchandise units in 23 countries.
CONSUMER TRENDS:
WASHINGTON - The "comfort food" of America's family-style restaurants -- meat loaf, patty melts, milkshakes and burgers -- is loaded with artery-clogging fat, a consumer watchdog group says.

LUXEMBOURG - Consumers must be clearly informed so that they can choose whether or not to buy genetically modified food, Austrian Farm Minister Wilhelm Molterer says. Food safety is a sensitive issue in Austria where last week over 1.2 million people signed a petition calling for a ban on the release of genetically modified organisms into food or the environment.
CAPE TOWN - South Africa's Consumers will soon be able to do their banking via the local supermarket as supermarket giants Pick 'n Pay and Shoprite-Checkers move into in-store banking.
